Digital estate planning in Australia: wills, executors and online accounts

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 15 Oct 2026

In Australia, your executor manages your estate, including digital assets, after you die. Many banks and platforms want a grant of probate or letters of administration from your state's Supreme Court before releasing money or data. Estates typically take 6 to 12 months. Leave an inventory, not passwords, with your will.

Key facts

  • Probate or letters of administration, if asset holders require them, is usually applied for within 6 months of death in NSW.
  • Estate administration typically takes 6 to 12 months (ATO).

What are the steps?

  1. Make or update a valid will and name an executor; NSW's guide notes this can be family, a friend, a solicitor or NSW Trustee and Guardian.
  2. List your digital assets: email, cloud storage, socials, PayPal, crypto exchanges, wallets, domains and subscriptions.
  3. Store logins in a password manager with emergency access rather than in the will.
  4. Switch on the free platform tools: Google Inactive Account Manager, Apple Legacy Contact, a Facebook legacy contact.
  5. After a death: get the death certificate, find the will, and notify organisations. The Australian Death Notification Service can notify several at once.
  6. Phone the ATO to pause tax correspondence and decide who will manage the deceased's affairs.
  7. Ask each asset holder whether they need a grant; small or jointly held assets may not.
  8. Apply to the Supreme Court in your state for probate (with a will) or letters of administration (without one) if needed.
  9. Collect assets, pay debts and tax, then distribute. In NSW, executors usually shouldn't distribute earlier than 6 months after death.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need probate for digital accounts in Australia?

It depends on the asset holder. The Supreme Court of Victoria says to ask each holder whether it needs a grant; PayPal Australia, for example, asks for a grant of probate or letters of administration.

How long does an estate take in Australia?

The ATO says administration typically takes 6 to 12 months but can take longer.

Does Apple need a court order in Australia?

Apple says Australia is one of the jurisdictions where it accepts alternative documentation instead of a court order.

Should I put passwords in my Australian will?

No. A will can be read by others after death. Keep passwords in a password manager with emergency access and keep an inventory with your will.

What is the difference between probate and letters of administration?

Probate is granted to the executor named in a valid will. Letters of administration are issued when there's no valid will, usually to the closest next of kin.
